stem: An arterial blood gas report shows a markedly negative base excess (base deficit). Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: It represents a relative deficit of metabolic base and supports a metabolic acidifying component when interpreted with pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate, and context.
options.B: It establishes an isolated respiratory acid-base disorder and makes a metabolic contribution unlikely regardless of the remaining ABG values.
options.C: It is a calculated value unrelated to metabolic acid-base status, so it does not contribute to interpretation of an abnormal ABG pattern.
options.D: It indicates normal acid-base balance even when the pH, PaCO2, or bicarbonate are abnormal and inconsistent with a normal interpretation.

rationale: The July 2026 StatPearls/NCBI ABG review identifies base excess/deficit as a calculated parameter representing a relative excess or deficit of base. A markedly negative value is therefore a base deficit and supports a metabolic acidifying component. The same source emphasizes systematic ABG interpretation using pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate, oxygenation, and clinical context rather than diagnosing an acid-base disorder from one calculated parameter alone. A is correct. B wrongly makes the finding purely respiratory, C dismisses its metabolic meaning, and D misclassifies an abnormal base deficit as normal.
educational_objective: Interpret a negative base excess as evidence of a metabolic base deficit while integrating it with the complete ABG rather than using it as a stand-alone diagnosis.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf) / StatPearls
source_document_title: Arterial Blood Gas Analysis: Fundamentals, Interpretation, and Clinical Utility
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; last update July 5, 2026; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Specimen Requirements/ABG components: base excess/deficit is a calculated relative excess or deficit of base. Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings: ABG interpretation is systematic using pH, PaCO2, bicarbonate and oxygenation with clinical correlation.
source_claim_supported: A markedly negative base excess represents a base deficit and supports a metabolic acidifying component but must be interpreted with the full ABG.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — interpretation of laboratory and diagnostic findings.
correction_summary: Removed 'always' cueing and balanced option lengths while preserving the distinction between a metabolic base deficit and a full acid-base diagnosis.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — the 2026 NCBI source defines base excess/deficit as a calculated base parameter and requires integrated ABG interpretation; A alone satisfies both points.
